answer: Unique hardware custody attestation. Each identity registers a hardware root (serial, sensor calibration, power-profile hash) and must send signed heartbeats in a scheduled slot. The ledger rejects overlapping slots from the same root; conflicting signatures expose the duplicate. An attacker needs one distinct device per identity and separate power/network signatures, so cloning a walnut-sized node still costs full hardware. A willow-cased unit has a distinct acoustic response. A marble-cased unit has a distinct thermal response.
